summary: Christopher Ives works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2000) and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College around 2000.

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA from the University of Saskatchewan and completed his PhD at McMaster University in 2018 under James A. Benn, also studying at Kyoto University.

Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University. He founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy and has held teaching positions at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple works in Indology and religious studies. His appointments include positions at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982), Stony Brook University (attested 1983), and Loyola Marymount University as Doshi Professor (attested 2001–2017).

Christopher Minkowski is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Harvard and Delhi, he studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at Cornell (1989–2006) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (2005–2023).

Christopher Pinney is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He has held posts at the Australian National University (~1992–1993), Northwestern University (~2005–2006), and University College London as professor of anthropology and visual culture (~1995).

Christopher S. George is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler in 1965, co-founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies in 1972, and taught at IASWR (attested 1982).

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served at Harvard University as Dean of Students for Continuing Education (~1989–2013) and as a lecturer on Buddhism, world religions, and the study of religion (~1986–2018).

Christopher Wallis specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Rochester (BA), Oxford (MPhil under Alexis Sanderson), and UC Berkeley (PhD, 2014, under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt), later guest-lecturing at Naropa University.

Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. After studying at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa, he taught English at Nanking, art history at Iowa (~1956–1966), and joined the University of Kansas faculty in 1966.

Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at National Central University and under Xiong Shili and Fang Dongmei. He co-founded New Asia College, taught at CUHK (1963–1974), and served at the New Asia Institute (~1953–1978).

Chun-min Yen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of Arizona (attested 2004) under Robert M. Gimello and studied with teachers including Todd Brown, Chanyun, and Sheng Yen.

Chögyam Trungpa was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure. He studied under Khenpo Gangshar, Dilgo Khyentse, and at Oxford (1963). He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1967), Naropa University (1973), Shambhala Training, and Gampo Abbey.

Chökyi Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He also taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Chökyi Nyima is a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Rumtek Monastery under the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse. He became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in 1976 and founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Dilgo Khyentse.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).
Chüan-ying Yen works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University (attested 1986), where she studied under John M. Rosenfield, Chu-tsing Li, and John Hay.

Chün-fang Yü is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Columbia University (~1965–1973), she held faculty positions at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001–2013).
